name: Metformin
dosage: 500mg to 1000mg, usually twice daily with meals
side_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, stomach upset, metallic taste. Usually improves after a few weeks.
interactions: Contrast dye used in some X-rays
plain_explanation: This medicine helps control blood sugar in type 2 diabetes. Take it with food to avoid an upset stomach.

name: Amlodipine
side_effects: Swelling in ankles/feet, dizziness, flushing, headache
plain_explanation: This medicine relaxes blood vessels to lower blood pressure. Take it at the same time each day.

name: Atorvastatin
dosage: 10mg to 80mg once daily, usually at night
side_effects: Muscle pain, joint pain, digestive issues
plain_explanation: This medicine lowers bad cholesterol to protect your heart. Report unexplained muscle pain to your doctor.

name: Aspirin
dosage: 75mg to 100mg once daily (low-dose, for heart protection)
side_effects: Stomach irritation, increased bleeding risk, heartburn
plain_explanation: This low-dose tablet helps prevent blood clots and protects your heart. Take it with food to protect your stomach.

name: Omeprazole
side_effects: Headache, stomach pain, nausea, long-term use may lower vitamin B12
plain_explanation: This medicine reduces stomach acid to prevent heartburn and protect your stomach lining. Take it on an empty stomach.

name: Levothyroxine
dosage: 25mcg to 200mcg once daily, on an empty stomach
side_effects: Rare at correct dose; too much can cause rapid heartbeat, anxiety, weight loss
plain_explanation: This medicine replaces a hormone your thyroid isn't making enough of. Take it first thing in the morning, at least 30 minutes before eating.

name: Losartan
interactions: Potassium supplements (risk of dangerously high potassium)
NSAIDs like ibuprofen (reduces effectiveness, affects kidneys)
plain_explanation: This medicine relaxes blood vessels to lower blood pressure and protect your kidneys. Take it at the same time each day.

name: Warfarin
dosage: Varies per person, based on regular blood tests (INR)
side_effects: Bruising, bleeding, requires regular blood monitoring
plain_explanation: This medicine prevents dangerous blood clots. It needs regular blood tests to get the dose right, and many foods/medicines can affect how well it works.

name: Insulin (Regular/NPH)
dosage: Varies per person, injected based on blood sugar readings
side_effects: Low blood sugar (shakiness, sweating, confusion), weight gain
interactions: Alcohol (increases risk of low blood sugar)
Beta-blockers (can hide low blood sugar symptoms)
plain_explanation: This is a hormone injection that controls blood sugar levels. Always eat after taking it to avoid your sugar dropping too low.

name: Paracetamol
dosage: 500mg to 1000mg every 4-6 hours, max 4000mg per day
side_effects: Generally safe at correct dose; overdose can cause serious liver damage
interactions: Warfarin (may slightly increase bleeding risk with regular high use)
plain_explanation: This is a common pain and fever reliever. Never exceed the daily maximum dose, as too much can seriously harm your liver.

name: Amoxicillin
dosage: 250mg to 500mg, 3 times daily, for the full prescribed course
plain_explanation: This antibiotic treats bacterial infections. Always finish the full course even if you feel better, or the infection can come back stronger.
